dimensions.label: Cheapest way to start
dimensions.a: $97 a month (Starter), unlimited users and contacts; no free plan, only a 14-day trial
dimensions.b: $0 forever (Free plan): 2,000 contacts, 3 sales funnels, 1 course, no card required

dimensions.label: Contacts allowed per plan
dimensions.a: Unlimited contacts on every plan, including the $97 Starter
dimensions.b: Tiered by plan: 2,000 (Free), 5,000 (Startup), 10,000 (Webinar); Unlimited's page calls contacts unlimited, though its plans API caps that plan at 1,000,000

dimensions.label: CRM and phone system
dimensions.a: Full CRM with pipelines, plus local and toll-free numbers, calls and SMS built in on every plan, billed per use from a prepaid wallet
dimensions.b: CRM pipelines included (up to 100 on Unlimited), but no built-in phone system; SMS needs your own connected Twilio account, billed at Twilio's rates

dimensions.label: Email sending
dimensions.a: Metered per email sent, about $0.675 per 1,000, with no monthly send cap on any plan
dimensions.b: Unlimited sends on every plan, including Free, with no per-email charge

dimensions.label: Funnels, sites and courses
dimensions.a: Website, funnel and landing-page builder plus courses and communities on every plan, positioned alongside the CRM and phone system rather than as the main feature
dimensions.b: Funnels, websites, blogs, courses and communities are the core product; funnel count is capped by plan, from 3 on Free to 50 on Webinar, with no cap listed on Unlimited

dimensions.label: Evergreen webinars
dimensions.a: Not listed as a plan feature or add-on on HighLevel's pricing or help-center pages
dimensions.b: 10 evergreen webinars included starting on the $47 Webinar plan; not available on Free or Startup

dimensions.label: Selling physical products
dimensions.a: No storefront or product-catalog feature listed in HighLevel's plans or add-ons
dimensions.b: A store for physical products is built in; variant caps run 50, 100 and 250 on Free, Startup and Webinar (Unlimited's plans API caps it at 5,000, though the pricing page calls it unlimited)

dimensions.label: Running client accounts and reselling
dimensions.a: Starter includes 3 sub-accounts; Unlimited ($297) rebills usage to clients at cost, and Agency Pro ($497) adds marked-up rebilling plus full SaaS resale
dimensions.b: Every plan, including Free, allows unlimited sub-accounts sharing the main plan's limits; systeme.io's own FAQ and help centre disagree on how its separate white-label pricing works

dimensions.label: Downgrading or canceling
dimensions.a: Upgrade, downgrade or cancel from the dashboard at any time; any unused wallet balance is forfeited 30 days after cancellation
dimensions.b: Upgrading is self-serve, but downgrading needs a support ticket and a custom order form; cancellation takes effect just before the next renewal

dimensions.label: AI features
dimensions.a: AI Employee add-on costs $50 or $97 per sub-account a month, plus pay-per-use conversation, voice and content AI beyond that
dimensions.b: No AI features listed on the pricing page or in the plan tables

verdicts.why: GoHighLevel's sub-accounts, phone system and CRM are built for an agency running several clients, with Unlimited and Agency Pro adding usage rebilling; Systeme.io's sub-accounts share the main plan's limits but come with no phone system or rebilling built for that job.

Systeme.io's funnels, unlimited email, courses and a free 2,000-contact plan are built around launching a course; GoHighLevel bundles courses too, but next to a CRM and phone system a course creator is unlikely to configure, behind a $97 floor Systeme.io's Free plan avoids entirely.

A Shopify-store owner already has checkout, inventory and shipping covered; neither GoHighLevel's CRM-and-funnel toolset nor Systeme.io's funnel-first store, capped at 50 to 5,000 product variants depending on plan, is built to replace a dedicated ecommerce platform.

A clinic, contractor or salon runs on booking, reviews and call-or-text follow-up, which GoHighLevel bundles into its CRM and phone system; Systeme.io has no built-in phone or SMS system, so texting a customer list means opening and paying for a separate Twilio account first.

A freelancer selling one offer through a funnel and email list fits Systeme.io's Free or $17 Startup plan, not GoHighLevel's $97 floor and usage wallet for a phone system and CRM sub-accounts a solo operator will not touch.

Neither platform bills or sells the way subscription software does; GoHighLevel is built around agency sub-accounts and client rebilling, and Systeme.io is built around funnels and one-time or recurring info-product sales, so a SaaS startup needs product-led signup and billing tools neither one provides.
